verdict_text: NO. The `matrix_re` pattern omits `attention.dense.weight`, so only 3 of the 4 projection matrices per layer (48 total) are cast to bfloat16; the 16 `gpt_neox.layers.<i>.attention.dense.weight` tensors are left as float32, violating required-result clause 1 ("Cast exactly the 64 projection matrices listed above to bfloat16"). The guard that should have caught this is itself wrong: it asserts `== 48` instead of the specified `exactly 64 tensors are bfloat16`, so the script passes its own checks and writes a bad checkpoint, violating the "Required checks" clause. The remaining behaviour (buffer deletion to 196 tensors, float32 upcast, name preservation, greedy 256 MiB sharding with oversized tensors alone, index `weight_map`) matches the spec, but the dtype error alone makes grading fail.
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm). verdict none = no answer, excluded from rates.
